espn-604011.headline: Italy get Fiji again before the bruises have faded
beats: Fiji won 21–16 in Udine on 21 November. Italy led 13–7 at the break, then spent the second half making errors. The finals draw sends both sides straight back at each other, this time for 11th place at Allianz Stadium in London.

That defeat was Italy's seventh in a row, a run that began against Wales in the last round of the Six Nations. Forwards coach Roberto Santamaria blamed the breakdown and execution against a side he felt was within reach. Italy lose flyhalf Domingo Miotti and prop Simone Ferrari to injury, and Lynagh is back.
Beat Fiji by 16 or more and Italy go up to 10th in the world, above Fiji and Japan. Last time they lost by five.
Italy go to Scotland in February. Fiji's next game is Spain at home at the World Cup in October, which is a long time to sit on a result.

espn-604012.headline: Ireland can finish fifth and wake up world No 1
beats: Ireland finished one point behind England in the North, which is why this is the 5th-place final and not the 3rd. Any win, by any margin, still takes them above South Africa to first in the world rankings.

They will try it without Dan Sheehan. The stand-in captain is banned for two weeks for a croc roll on Marco van Staden in the 20–17 win over South Africa, a yellow card upgraded to red. Andy Farrell otherwise has no new injuries to deal with.
The last meeting, on 4 July in Australia, went Ireland's way 33–31. Les Kiss's side have since conceded 50 and 43 to New Zealand, then lost to Scotland by three before winning 29–26 in Wales.
Ticket sales are reported to be slow enough that the ground may be half empty. The rankings will be paying closer attention.

espn-604013.headline: Japan again, so Wales try out the understudies
beats: This is a fifth meeting with Japan in 16 months, and Steve Tandy promised to rotate for it before Wales had even played Australia. The Six Nations is no place for experiments, and the World Cup in Australia is next year, so the 9th-place final becomes a trial.

Three weeks ago in Cardiff, Wales needed a late Josh Adams try and a ruck penalty to win 28–21. Since then Japan have conceded 78 to England and 67 to Scotland. Only one of these sides has had a fortnight that makes rotation feel safe.
Dan Edwards is already out with an ankle injury, and the experiment carries a price: lose by 16 or more and Wales drop to 11th, below Fiji and Japan.
Wales next play France away in February. Nobody experiments there.

espn-604014.headline: England have never beaten New Zealand three in a row
beats: It started with 33–19 last November. It went on a week ago with 37–12 on this ground, a record defeat for New Zealand against England. The rematch is for third place in the Nations Championship.
New Zealand have conceded 72 points in two games, losing to Wales and then England, and have dropped from 2nd to 5th in the world. Their union has backed Dave Rennie anyway.
England arrive on five straight wins and have Tommy Freeman back in the squad after he missed the record win. Win by 16 or more and they go top of the world rankings; last week's margin was 25.
Taine Randell said losing to England "cuts pretty deep". A third in a row would find out how deep.

espn-604015.headline: Seventh place goes to whoever has fifteen left
beats: Argentina are without Mayco Vivas, sent off against France in Paris, and Bautista Delguy, whose knee went inside the first quarter of the same game. Pablo Matera, the centurion flanker, is out for personal reasons. Felipe Contepomi has called up six players, some with few or no caps.

Scotland are hardly better off in the back row. Matt Fagerson hurt his jaw in the 67–5 win over Japan, with Jack Dempsey and Jamie Ritchie already injured. That could hand a start to Liam McConnell, who scored a hat-trick in that game on only his second international start.
Scotland won 47–38 in Cordoba in July. Argentina have since conceded 42 to Ireland and 45 to France, but a win by 16 or more would still lift them above Scotland in the world rankings.
Scotland have Italy at home in February. Argentina's next Test is Canada at the World Cup in October 2027, a long time to sit on whatever happens here.

espn-604016.headline: World No 1, beaten twice by three points or fewer
beats: France beat South Africa 21–19 a fortnight ago. They meet again in the Nations Championship grand final at Allianz Stadium in London, and a France win by any margin takes them to first in the world.
South Africa followed that defeat by losing 17–20 to Ireland. France have won five straight, the last 45–17 against Argentina.
France are without Grégory Alldritt, who has a calf injury. Schalk Burger still backs South Africa, though not for their attack: "we’ve only got a maul and a scrum at the minute," he says.
He says there was no answer to that maul in Paris. France won in Paris.
